$comment: Expected fp1 fingerprints. See fp1/README.md before editing.

fixtures.expect: A plain chart: hi-hat, snare and bass drum over two measures, with a BGM line that must not count.
Three lines on channel 12 in measure 1, at K=2, K=3 and K=2 again. They overlay to the union {0/1, 1/3, 1/2}, each line read at its own K; they are never concatenated into one line.
Onsets written on the coarsest grid that holds them.
The same onsets as fp1-subdivision-coarse re-saved on finer grids (K=192, 4, 6 and 16). Positions are reduced fractions, so the fingerprint must not move.
The same onsets as fp1-relabel-original with every code relabelled (0A, ZZ) and the WAV definitions renamed. A code is an onset unless it is exactly 00, so nothing moves.
A chart with #BPM and #BPM01 set, and a channel 08 tempo change.
fp1-bpm-slow with only the #BPM and #BPM01 values changed. Positions are measure-relative, so a tempo edit moves no onset.
Onsets in measures 0, 2, 10, 99 and 999 and nowhere between; measure 5 has an all-00 line that contributes nothing. Measures sort by number, so 10 follows 2.
Channels 1A, 1B and 1C, written out of order and once in lower case with spaces in the payload. Lanes serialise in canonical order 11 to 1C.
BGM, measure length, guitar, bass, auto-play and hidden channels, and an all-00 drum line. No player-struck drum onset, so there is no fingerprint: fp1 is null, which is not a sentinel.
Lines of K=5, 7, 11 and 47, whose onsets do not land on any power-of-two grid (a 384-per-measure store cannot hold a fifth).
A UTF-16LE file with a byte-order mark and a Japanese title.
Shift-JIS with a double-byte title, a lead byte with no trail byte before a CRLF, and a lead byte directly before the # of an object line, which stops that line being read as one.
UTF-8 with a byte-order mark. A U+00A0 inside a payload is white space and is removed; a U+0085 is not white space to the reference and stays, shifting how the payload pairs into codes.
